study_identification_part.si4_title: Detecting accelerated retinal decline in mental disorders through normative modeling

study_characteristics_part.sc1_study_objective: To estimate age-related decline of the human retina using normative modeling in healthy controls and compare it to the decline seen in schizophrenia, bipolar disorder, and major depression, testing the hypothesis that mental disorders involve accelerated retinal decline.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa7_association_analysis: Linear models (lm) with retinal thickness metric deviations (z-scores) as dependent variable and diagnostic group and sex as predictor variables; chi-squared tests for enrichment of extreme values (infranormal and supranormal) comparing rates between groups; alpha set at 0.05; nominal p-values reported; robustness checks with extended covariate models including BMI, smoking, alcohol, diabetes, socioeconomic status; permutation analysis (250 iterations) with 3:1 HC to patient ratio for linear model comparisons; effect sizes reported as Cohen's d for linear models; mixed models for repeated measures (left and right eyes) to account for laterality
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa8_key_findings_brief: Mental disorders, particularly schizophrenia and bipolar disorder, showed accelerated retinal decline compared to normative models, with negative deviations in macular thickness and GC-IPL but not RNFL, and enrichment of infranormal values.
clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa9_key_findings_detailed: Normative models revealed curve-like age-related retinal decline more pronounced in males. Mental disorders showed significantly negative deviations in macular thickness (z=-0.29, P<0.0001) and GC-IPL (z=-0.18, P<0.0001) but not RNFL. Effects were driven by SZ (macular z=-0.47, P<0.0001; GC-IPL z=-0.24, P=0.001) and BD (macular z=-0.23, P<0.0001; GC-IPL z=-0.16, P=0.004), with SZ showing more pronounced thinning than BD in outer temporal (Δz=-0.26, P=0.0022) and outer inferior (Δz=-0.19, P=0.0288) macular subfields. MDD showed no significant deviations. Extreme value analysis showed enrichment of infranormal values in mental disorders for macular thickness (4.65% vs 2.03% in controls, p=0.0003) and GC-IPL (4.83% vs 2.35%, p=0.0002). Inner macular subfields showed more pronounced effects than central and outer subfields. Results were robust to cardiovascular covariate adjustment and permutation testing.

caa10_key_limitations.answer: Limited to mid-to-late lifespan (UK Biobank age range); cross-sectional design without repeated measurements in same individuals for comprehensive understanding of age-related decline; normative models focused on specific age range leaving early-life retinal changes outside scope
caa10_key_limitations.supporting_text: There are two limitations that merit comment. First, because we relied on data from the UK Biobank, our normative models focused on the mid- to late lifespan, leaving early-life retinal changes outside the scope of this analysis. Although this limited the age range we could model, the large, standardized dataset with high quality phenotyping minimized measurement error and ensured consistency. Second, a more comprehensive understanding of age-related retinal decline would benefit from repeated measurements in the same individuals.

clinical_application_and_analysis_part.caa11_application_notes: Sex-specific normative curves were generated by building sex- and laterality-specific models. Z-scores from left and right eyes were averaged for downstream analyses, with robustness checks using mixed models for repeated measures. Interaction effects between age, sex, and laterality were explored in supplementary analyses. Outlier removal performed separately within control and patient groups to preserve disease-related deviations. IQR multiplier robustness analysis performed across range 1-7. Extended analysis with cardiovascular covariates confirmed main findings. Permutation approach with matched 3:1 HC:patient ratio used to validate findings against simple linear models.

general_note_part.gn1_general_notes: This is a preprint (medRxiv) not yet peer-reviewed. The study focuses on retinal imaging (OCT) rather than traditional neuroimaging, but applies normative modeling framework to detect accelerated neurodegeneration in mental disorders. The retina is conceptualized as an extension of brain tissue accessible through non-invasive imaging. Measurements include total macular thickness, 9 coronal subfields (central, 4 inner, 4 outer), and 2 cellular sublayers (RNFL, GC-IPL). All participants from single dataset (UK Biobank) with standardized OCT protocol. Diagnoses based on ICD-10 codes (F20 for SZ, F31 for BD, F33 for MDD). Additional robustness check examined 29,025 individuals with self-reported depressive symptoms lasting >1 week. Code availability: https://github.com/homanlab/ (after publication).
